argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: explicitly stated as Premise 1, Premise 2, Conclusion

argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: low to moderate for Premise 1; high for Premise 2 as analytic conditional

explicit_definitions_given: Turing Test: operational test based on indistinguishability in verbal behavior
M1: pure lookup table storing all possible conversation branches
M2: compressed database / statistical model approximating human linguistic data
Psychologism: intelligence requires specific internal psychological/conscious states
Intentional stance: treating an entity as an intentional agent when behavior is best predicted by attributing beliefs/desires

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: directly addresses objections by reinterpreting M2 as functional realization and dismissing M1 as physically impossible
objections_raised: M1 is physically impossible due to combinatorial explosion
M2, when feasible, is no longer a mere lookup table but a functional information-processing system
The intuition that M1/M2 lacks intelligence is unreliable and collapses under unbounded conversational competence

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: thought experiments, conceptual analysis, appeals to physical constraints, appeals to pragmatic methodology

philosophical_orientation.sentiment: critical of Block, sympathetic to Turing and Dennett
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: philosophy of mind, artificial intelligence, Turing Test, functionalism, intentional stance

structural_organization.structure_type: sections with numbered subsections and explicit transitions

summary_of_core_decisions: The essay reconstructs Block's argument as a valid syllogism, then attacks Premise 1 by showing M1 is physically impossible and M2 is question-begging when made feasible. It further undermines the intuition supporting Premise 1 by imagining an unbounded conversational machine (Block-Omega) and arguing that the attribution of intelligence becomes rationally mandatory. The conclusion is that Block's rejection of the Turing Test is unsound.
